concept: Link prints a reference the way a manual does: the words stay in the sentence's own ink and size, and one thin rule runs under them so nobody has to guess what can be pressed. A link already read steps one ink lighter, and a link that leaves the app carries one small dot-matrix mark at its end.

default_to_avoid.pattern: a link in the brand accent colour with no rule under it, an underline appearing only on hover
default_to_avoid.why_not: Colour alone tells it from the text around it, which fails for anyone who cannot see the hue, and the accent colour would spend the unit's one orange on a reference.

default_to_avoid.pattern: a link styled as a button: a filled pill or a bordered box with an arrow
default_to_avoid.why_not: A pill reads as a key that does something here. A link goes somewhere, and dial keeps keys for things you turn or press.

references.source: Braun instruction manuals (Ulm school, 1960s): cross-references printed in the running text with a plain rule under the page number, no colour
WCAG 2.2 1.4.1 Use of Color: a link inside text needs a cue that is not colour
WCAG 2.2 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum): a link inside a sentence is exempt, a link on its own line is not

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: A link is ink on plastic in every state, and its mark and rule are ink too. The unit's one orange stays on its primary control.

derivation.consequence: ink on plastic at ≥4.5:1 in both themes
derivation.form: Rest is primary ink and a link already read is secondary ink, both measured above 4.5:1 on the page and the body in light and dark.
A link has no size or weight of its own. It takes the size and line height of the sentence it stands in, so a Thai line keeps its room.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: A link on its own line is 44px tall and at least the touch width. A link inside a sentence stays the height of the line, because WCAG exempts it and 44px boxes would break the paragraph.

derivation.consequence: no hover lift; hover only darkens a key's ink a step
derivation.form: A link is already in the darkest ink, so there is no step to darken. The rule under it thickens one step and nothing lifts, moves or changes size.

derivation.consequence: fast in, slow out, through the state motion tokens
derivation.form: The rule thickens over the hover token and settles back on the same easing; under Reduce motion it changes at once.

options.name: solid rule under ink text, thickens on hover
dotted leader as the rule, solid on hover
no rule at rest, ink bar on hover only

variants.reason: A tells a link at rest by a shape that survives a grey screen, and keeps the text in the sentence's own ink. B breaks on wrapped lines and its ring-ink dots are too faint under small type. C shows nothing until hover, which touch screens never get and WCAG 1.4.1 does not accept.

link.why: A plain anchor, so the browser keeps its own open, copy and new-tab behaviour. It inherits the sentence's size, weight and line height and adds one rule under the words.

standalone.why: A link on its own line, such as All lamps. It is a row 44px tall and at least the touch width, with the rule under the words only.

mark.why: The dot-matrix share glyph at the end of an external link. It is named for assistive tech, so the new tab is announced, and it is ink like the words.

hover.why: Hover thickens the rule from a hairline to the ring width. The words stay in place and the rule is the only part that answers.

focus-visible.why: Keyboard focus draws the same dark ring around the link as on every part of the system, offset so it clears the descenders.

data-visited.why: A link already read prints one ink step lighter and its rule turns dotted. Browsers only let CSS change colour on a visited link, so the dotted rule comes from the visited prop, which a router can set.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduce motion the rule changes thickness at once, with no transition.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the link takes the system link and visited colours, and the rule stays because it is a text decoration.

text-decoration-thickness.why: The rule thickens over 120ms and settles back over 240ms on the decelerating curve (motion.hover with kiln.state), fast in and slow out; nothing travels.

color.why: The ink step between a link and a visited link fades over the same hover token, because a colour fade moves nothing.
